title: soft-slo-quantile-trimmer-and-egress-fence-hotfix
author: Evan Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: Add soft-quantile SLO throttler to reduce circuit flip oscillations; introduce egress fence to isolate aggressive global egress cuts from cold regions; tweak inflight hedging backoff. Improves stability during regional egress spikes and reduces tenant impact.
description:
Context: During the outage on 2026-02-10 (Linear ENG-2145) we observed repeated circuit flips driven by an aggressive egress cap that applied globally and a hard percentile cut at the SLO boundary. Cold regions with low KV cache pressure were being forced into slowpaths which then tripped regional circuits and cascaded. This PR introduces a soft-quantile SLO throttler that smooths enforcement around the target percentile and an egress fence policy that prevents aggressive global egress reductions from immediately affecting regions with divergent capacity profiles.

What this PR does (single-string description): Implements a soft quantile throttler in services/scheduler that uses a sigmoid-based smoothing window around configured SLO percentiles, adds an egress fence layer in services/egress that marks region eligibility for global egress reductions and enforces staged application, tunes inflight hedging backoff to use exponential backoff with jitter to avoid herd replays, and surfaces additional telemetry (slo_trim_count, egress_fence_denied, inflight_replay_rate) for post-deploy analysis. Includes unit and integration tests, a small canary rollout plan, and a rollback toggle.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2145/soft-quantile-slo-throttler (high-level design and math) - [x] Unit tests for throttler smoothing behavior and egress fence acceptance logic - [x] Integration test for staged egress application in staging cluster - [x] Canary deployment (10% regional routes) observed for 24h with no regression - [x] Added telemetry and dashboards for quick triage - [x] Rollback toggle added (feature flag: slo.soft_trimmer.enabled)

Performance expectations: smoothing reduces spike-induced throttle variance by ~40% in internal microbenchmarks and reduces circuit reopen frequency under synthetic egress bursts. Egress fence should prevent 70% of global egress policy applications from touching cold regions immediately (measured in synthetic staging run). See bench results in commits.

Rollback and safety: feature flag can disable new throttler and egress fence immediately; implementation defaults to fallthrough mode that preserves current behavior if the flag is off. No datastore migrations. Metric-backed abort: if slo_trim_count or inflight_replay_rate exceed safety thresholds we will automatically disable via the feature-flag operator.

Commits summary: - Add soft-quantile throttler core algorithm and tests (author) - Add egress fence policy with staged-apply logic and tests (author) - Tune inflight hedging backoff and add jitter (author) - Add telemetry counters and Grafana dashboard snippets (author) - Canary rollout scripts and config (ops)

Changed areas (high-level): services/scheduler/throttler.go -> new smoothing algorithm and config options; services/egress/policy.go -> egress fence acceptance and staged apply; runtime/kv/cache_manager.go -> small guard to avoid triggering egress fence during KV drain; observability/metrics/registry.go -> new counters and tags; infra/canary/deploy.yaml -> canary rollout config; tests/integration/egress_staged_apply_test.go -> integration test for staged policy.

Why this is different from prior work: Existing SLO enforcement applied a hard percentile cutoff which produced brittle transitions when load and egress quotas were noisy. This change pushes enforcement to a soft window and complements it with a policy-level fence to keep cold regions insulated from large global adjustments. It is intended as an operational stability improvement rather than a new feature.

Related: Linear ENG-2145 (incident), SRE-671 (postmortem follow-up), SUP-982 (customer report about regional flapping).
